findings.description: The DB master password (var.password) and the RDS endpoint, username and database name are written in cleartext into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc on the instance via user_data, which only root can read but is also stored in EC2 instance metadata where any local user or SSRF can retrieve it; the same password is the master credential for the RDS instance.

publicly_accessible = true assigns a public IP/DNS name to the RDS instance, exposing MySQL to the internet. Combined with the wide string-concatenated queries in the app it materially increases attack surface.
storage_encrypted = false leaves the RDS storage, automated backups and snapshots unencrypted; the database holds application data protected only by account-level controls.

The instance role policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", giving the EC2 instance full control of S3, EC2 and RDS in the account. Any compromise of the web server (which runs a PHP app with SQL string concatenation) yields full control-plane access.

The DB security group allows all egress to 0.0.0.0/0 on all ports and protocols (protocol -1, ports 0-0), enabling unrestricted outbound traffic and data exfiltration from the database security group.
MySQL port 3306 is opened to the entire VPC CIDR, so any host in the VPC (not just the catalog app server) can reach the database; the intended source should be the app security group.
The RDS master username is the well-known default "admin", which lowers the effort required for credential-guessing attacks against the database.

findings.issue_category: no permissions boundary on instance role
findings.description: The EC2 assumable role has no permissions boundary or condition restricting use, so it can be assumed by any EC2 instance in the account and carries the full wildcard policy attached to it.

The user_data script embeds the database password inline (define('DB_PASSWORD', '${var.password}')) and is stored in instance user data and cloud-init logs; this leaks the RDS master credential to anyone with metadata access or console read permissions.
backup_retention_period = 0 disables automated backups and point-in-time recovery, so a destructive event or ransomware incident on the database is unrecoverable.
